thread:
maya: quick proposal — i'd like to try a "progressive validation" flow for new model intake today. idea: split into tiny stages so we can fail fast and collect signals without running full bench for everything.

sasha: +1. can you sketch the stages?

maya: sketch: 1) quick metadata lint + shape check (~30s) 2) microbench (1–5 mins, 10 requests) for perf regression 3) compatibility probe (runtime smoke: kv cache, tokenization, outputs) 4) golden-set eval for quality 5) full bench / certification if earlier stages pass.

liam: sounds reasonable. question: who kicks off the microbench and where does it run? bench infra or intake job?

maya: preference is intake service triggers a preflight job on the bench cluster with a small headroom quota. advantage: we get immediate signal and avoid queuing in full bench. downside: more surface area in intake code.

noah: tradeoff: if intake triggers bench, we need quota controls or noisy models will spin up many microjobs. maybe a centralized orchestrator that intake posts to? intake -> orchestrator -> bench. orchestrator can throttle and pick region.

sasha: orchestrator seems right. also we should codify pass/fail conditions for each stage. example rules: metadata lint must be green; microbench must not regress tail-p99 more than 30% vs baseline; compatibility probe must not throw runtime errors on 99% of golden prompts.

liam: for the microbench baseline — use the closest family baseline (e.g., Llama2-13B quantized) or model-specific golden? how do we pick baseline?

maya: heuristic: choose the most similar hosted model we have in the catalog. fallback to family baseline. store baseline fingerprint with each model record.

intake-bot: triggered probe job: probe-1770135791-01 queued on bench-cluster. link: https://bench.internal/jobs/1770135791

noah: we also need to consider caching/warmup for KV-heavy models. If the probe runs cold, latency will look worse. maybe probe should do a short warmup sequence (20 requests) before measuring.

sasha: agreed. include warmup+stabilization window in microbench stage. also add a separate kv-health check that exercises cache hits and misses.

liam: what about fail-open vs fail-closed? i.e., if compatibility probe times out but metadata lint passed, do we allow model to proceed into canary serving?

maya: i'd prefer fail-closed for production promotion — must pass compatibility to go to dedicated/canary. But we can allow a "developer-preview" bucket for manual overrides with audit log.

noah: automation: orchestrator should emit a compact signal object: {stage: name, status: pass|warn|fail, metrics: [...], artifacts: [links]} so UI and alerts can parse.
sasha: +1 — also store golden inputs and sample outputs in model record for future regression comparison.

liam: minor: we need a small contract for the probe harness API. something like: POST /probe with model-id, stage, budget_ms, input-set-id. response: job-id, estimated-duration.

maya: i'll draft an RFC for orchestrator API + minimal probe contract. will include YAML sketch for stages and pass/fail thresholds. snippet: ```yaml
stages:
  - name: lint
    timeout: 30s
    criteria: [metadata_ok]
  - name: microbench
    timeout: 5m
    warmup: 20
    criteria: [p99 <= baseline * 1.3]
  - name: compatibility
    timeout: 3m
    criteria: [runtime_errors == 0, tokenization_match >= 99]
  - name: golden_eval
    timeout: 10m
    criteria: [quality >= threshold]
```

intake-bot: draft rfc created: https://go/repo/rfcs/1770135791-progressive-validation (maya).

noah: can we also expose a "fast-fail" flag so teams can run only the lint+compat probe during high volume intake windows to reduce cost?

maya: yes — orchestrator will support stage selection and budgets. default full flow runs all stages.

sasha: next steps: maya to send RFC + contract PR; liam to prototype probe API on bench side; noah to scope orchestrator throttling and quota model; i'll write the criteria doc for golden inputs.

maya: thanks — i'll post RFC by EOD and schedule a short sync if folks want to pair on the prototype. :thumbsup:

liam: SGTM.

noah: 👍

sasha: thanks! great direction.
